title: Maps from qcqs scheme limits to a locally finitely presented algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $Z$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume that $Z\to S$ is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Then restriction induces a bijection of sets $$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Mor}_S(U_i,Z)\;\xrightarrow{\sim}\;\operatorname{Mor}_S(U,Z).$$ The colimit is the filtered colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: any map from $U$ factors through a stage $U_i$, and two stage maps to $Z$ induce the same map from $U$ if and only if they agree at a sufficiently late common stage. No finite-presentation hypothesis on the $U_i\to S$, and no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on $Z$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04AK (proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation), and Tag 0CP4 (lemma-better-characterize-relative-limit-preserving), applied to Z -> S and to inverse systems of schemes, viewed as algebraic spaces over S.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] with $P$ local finite presentation, the hypothesis on $Z\to S$ gives that for every scheme $V$ with a surjective etale map $V\to S$ and every scheme $W$ with a surjective etale map $W\to Z\times_SV$, the scheme morphism $W\to V$ is locally of finite presentation; this is the chart condition of [lem-sfb-space-relative-affine-limit-criterion]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-affine-limit-criterion] to $Z\to S$, with $S$ the terminal algebraic space over itself. For each $S$-scheme $T$ the set $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,S)$ is a singleton. Its colimit over a nonempty directed set is again a singleton: all stage representatives become equal at a common upper bound. The fibre product in the criterion is therefore $\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Z)$. Thus for every directed affine system $T=\varprojlim T_i$ the map $\operatorname{colim}\operatorname{Mor}_S(T_i,Z)\to\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,Z)$ is bijective. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], every map descends and equality of two stage maps is detected at a common later stage.

source.place: Tags 04AK and 06BC, applied with X=Z and Y=S

proof.text: Fix $i_0\in I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings] choose finitely many affine opens $A_{a,0}$ covering $U_{i_0}$, with quasi-compact pairwise intersections. For every pair choose a finite affine open cover $B_{ab,c,0}$ of $A_{a,0}\cap A_{b,0}$ by [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open]. For $j\ge i_0$ denote inverse images in $U_j$ by $A_{a,j}$ and $B_{ab,c,j}$, and inverse images in $U$ by $A_a$ and $B_{ab,c}$. They are affine by the definition [pqf-def-affine-morphism], since transitions and limit projections are affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] each $A_a$ and $B_{ab,c}$ is the limit of the corresponding affine inverse-image system. Inverse images preserve unions and intersections, so these remain covers at every stage and at the limit. The tail is small, nonempty and directed. Restricting to it changes neither the limit nor the eventual-equality test: any index and $i_0$ have a common upper bound.

source.place: Tag 0CP4 (lemma-better-characterize-relative-limit-preserving), scheme-source version of its two covering paragraphs

proof.text: Let $g:U\to Z$. Step 1 applied to each affine system $A_{a,j}$ descends $g|_{A_a}$ to some $g_{a,j_a}:A_{a,j_a}\to Z$. A common upper bound of the finitely many $j_a$ gives one stage $j$ and maps $g_{a,j}$. On each $B_{ab,c,j}$ the restrictions of $g_{a,j}$ and $g_{b,j}$ become equal on $B_{ab,c}$ because both are restrictions of $g$. The injectivity in step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] give a later stage for each equality. There are only finitely many triples $(a,b,c)$, so choose one $k\ge j$ where all these equalities hold. This uses affine tests on the selected $B$'s, and does not assume the whole overlap is affine.

source.place: Tag 0CP4, finite descent of sections and compatibility in the equalizer argument

proof.text: The algebraic space $Z$ is a sheaf on the big fppf site by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Every open cover used here is an fppf cover by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. The uniqueness part of the sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] first shows that the two restrictions on $A_{a,k}\cap A_{b,k}$ agree, since they agree on its covering $\{B_{ab,c,k}\}_c$. The existence part then glues the $g_{a,k}$ to a unique $g_k:U_k\to Z$. Its restriction to $U$ equals $g$ by uniqueness on the cover $\{A_a\}_a$. All sections are evaluated on $S$-schemes, so the glued morphism is over $S$. This proves surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0CP4, sheaf equalizer description of morphisms from the covered source

proof.text: Suppose $h_i:U_i\to Z$ and $h_j:U_j\to Z$ have equal restrictions to $U$. Choose a common stage $l\ge i,j$ and, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings], a finite affine open cover $\{A_{a,l}\}_a$ of $U_l$. For $m\ge l$ the inverse images $A_{a,m}\subseteq U_m$ and $A_a\subseteq U$ are affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism], since transitions and limit projections are affine, and $A_a=\varprojlim_{m\ge l}A_{a,m}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]; they cover $U_m$ and $U$. On each affine inverse-image system, the injective affine test of step 1 gives equality of the two restricted maps at a later stage. Directedness gives one later stage for the finitely many affine opens. The uniqueness part of the sheaf condition then makes the two maps on that stage equal. Conversely, equality at a stage remains equality after restriction to $U$. The representative and equality clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] now prove injectivity of the canonical colimit map and its stated interpretation. The argument also covers empty sources: the empty covering has exactly one matching family, hence the sheaf has one section there.

source.place: Tag 0CP4, injectivity in the equalizer argument and eventual equality
